item.title: Zim government appoints National Arts Council board
item.description: The government of Zimbabwe has appointed a new board to lead the National Arts Council of Zimbabwe (NACZ), effective 1 December 2025. The appointment was made by the Minister of Sport, Recreation, Arts and Culture, Anselem Sanyatwe. The board will run for four years until 30 November 2029, following a formal announcement by the Ministry of Sport, Recreation, Arts and Culture. item.title: Open call: MTN Bushfire Firefly 2025/2026 competition in eSwatini
item.description: Emerging artists from eSwatini are invited to submit applications for the 9th edition of the MTN Bushfire Firefly music talent competition. With support from MTN eSwatini, the programme is aimed at identifying and promoting new musical talent. It is open to vocalists, singers and rappers seeking wider exposure and professional development through live performance, mentorship and industry engagement. item.title: YouTube introduces video viewing recap feature for users
item.description: YouTube has launched a new personalised recap tool that summarises users’ viewing activity over the past year, offering a breakdown of watch history, preferred content types and changes in viewing patterns. The feature, called YouTube Recap, presents users with up to 12 information cards that highlight their most-watched channels, dominant interests and notable shifts in content consumption. item.title: Spotify Wrapped 2025: Kabza De Small dominates SA streams again
item.description: Amapiano artist Kabza De Small is once again the most streamed South African artist, with nearly 200 million streams. DJ Maphorisa reached close to 155 million streams, driven in part by the popularity of ‘Abantwana Bakho’ featuring Thatohatsi, Young Stunna and Nkosazana Daughter. Kelvin Momo recorded more than 71 million streams. His albums Ntsako and Thato Ya Modimo placed in the top 10 most-streamed albums. item.title: AI in music: A powerful tool, but who really owns the song?
item.description: Artificial intelligence is quietly, and sometimes loudly, changing the way music is made. With platforms like SUNO and Udio, it now takes seconds to generate melodies, lyrics and even complete songs. What once required studio time, musicians and long creative sessions can now happen with a few well-chosen prompts. For South African artists, this is both exciting and unsettling. item.title: Spotify Wrapped 2025: Wizkid is the most-streamed artist in Nigeria
item.description: Nigerian Afrobeats star Wizkid emerged as the most-streamed artist in Nigeria, followed by Seyi Vibez, Asake, Burna Boy and ODUMODUBLVCK. BNXN, FOLA, Davido, Rema and Olamide completed the top ten, underscoring the continued dominance of Afrobeats, street-hop and related genres in the local market. Ayra Starr retained her position as the most-streamed female artist in the country, ahead of Tems and Smur Lee. item.title: Bien, Sauti Sol and Wakadinali top Kenya’s Spotify Wrapped 2025 rankings
item.description: For the second consecutive year, Bien, Sauti Sol and Wakadinali remain among the most-streamed Kenyan artists on Spotify, continuing a run that has seen them feature consistently in the country’s top 10. They performed strongly alongside international acts, including Drake and Kendrick Lamar, who ranked first and third respectively among all artists streamed in Kenya during 2025. item.title: GWM marks 18 years in South Africa with FAM Fest at Syringa Park
item.description: GWM South Africa marked its 18th anniversary on 31 November with the launch of FAM Fest, a public event held at Syringa Park in Muldersdrift that combined live music, vehicle showcases and family-focused activities. item.title: Late Solly Moholo to receive Lifetime Achievement Award at SAMAs
item.description: The late South African artist Solomon Majafela Molokoane, known professionally as Solly Moholo, will be honoured with a posthumous Lifetime Achievement Award at the 31st South African Music Awards (SAMAs), scheduled to take place on 14 December. The announcement was made by the Recording Industry of South Africa (RiSA), which oversees the annual ceremony. item.title: LYFE Festival 2025 to bring Sabrina Claudio, Lloyiso and Manana to Joburg
item.description: Johannesburg is set to host LYFE Festival 2025 on 6 December, an event that will bring together elements of R&B, soul and contemporary African sounds. Scheduled to take place at Marks Park, the festival places a spotlight on the growing intersection between local and international music influences in South Africa’s urban centres.
